(17 May 2017) | attendance = 1,399,728 | average attendance = 4,604 | matches = 306 | total goals = 1037 | prevseason = [[2016 Thai League|2016]] | nextseason = [[2018 Thai League|2018]] | updated = 18 November 2017 }} The '''2017 [[Thai League T1]]''' (also known as the '''Toyota Thai League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 21st season of the Thai League, the top Thai professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1996. A total of 18 teams will compete in the league. The season began on 11 February 2017. Fixtures for the 2017 season were announced on 12 January 2017. [[Muangthong United F.C.|Muangthong United]] are the defending champions, having won the Thai Premier League title the [[2016 Thai Premier League|previous season]]. [[Thai Honda Ladkrabang F.C.|Thai Honda Ladkrabang]], [[Ubon UMT United F.C.|Ubon UMT United]] and [[Port F.C.|Port]] have entered as the three promoted teams from the [[2016 Thai Division 1 League|2016 Thai League 2]]. ==Changes from last season== ===Team changes=== ====From Thai League==== :'''Relegated to [[2017 Thai League 2]]''' :* [[Army United F.C.|Army United]] :* [[Chainat Hornbill F.C.|Chainat Hornbill]] :* [[BBCU F.C.|BBCU]] ====To Thai League==== :'''Promoted from [[2016 Thai Division 1 League]]''' :* [[Thai Honda Ladkrabang F.C.|Thai Honda Ladkrabang]] :* [[Ubon UMT United F.C.|Ubon UMT United]] :* [[Port F.C.|Port]] ===Stadium changes=== *[[BEC Tero Sasana F.C.|BEC Tero Sasana]] used the [[Boonyachinda Stadium]], a change from the previous season where they used the [[72nd Anniversary Stadium]] as their home ground in 2016. *[[Ubon UMT United F.C.|Ubon UMT United]] used the [[UMT Stadium]], a change from the previous season where they used the [[Tung Burapha Stadium]] as their home ground in 2016. ==Teams== There are 18 clubs in the league, with three promoted teams from [[Thai League 2]] replacing the three teams that were relegated from [[Thai League T1]] following the [[2016 Thai League T1|2016 season]]. All clubs that secured Thai League status for the season were subject to approval by the AFC Club Licensing before becoming eligible to participate. [[Army United F.C.|Army United]], [[Chainat Hornbill F.C.|Chainat Hornbill]] and [[BBCU F.C.|BBCU]] were relegated at the end of the 2016 season after finishing in the bottom three places of the table. They were replaced by [[2016 Thai Division 1 League|2016 Thai League 2]] champions [[Thai Honda Ladkrabang F.C.|Thai Honda Ladkrabang]], 2nd place [[Ubon UMT United F.C.|Ubon UMT United]] and 3rd place [[Port F.C.|Port]], were promoted to bring the total teams in the league to 18.
